claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features multiplayer support allowing players to manage products and make deals together.

citations.review_text: I would classify this as a cozy game. Make deals. Grow/mix your product. Weve played several hours in multiplayer with little to no bugs/glitching. Multiplayer controls are nice allowing all members to make deals, do runs, manage products etc. Take a shopkeep game with exploration and make it adult.

schedule 1 is a very charming game. Some might see it as friendslop and there is some elements of that but at its core, it is a very entertaining sandbox management game. trying to optimize selling your goods, unlocking new things to optimize that better, escaping cops, getting pissed at your customers its a game that has alot to keep you engaged. I feel that theres also alot of different ways to play this game too. You wanna become a kingpin all by yourself? Well theres alot of autamation you can do to help with that. You wanna play with friends? Well you guys can manually set up your empire as well. The game doesn't put too much pressure on you so you can play in your own way and have alot of laughs along the way too with its funny physics, random effects each of the substances give you and just how funny everything looks.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-game players find the content repetitive and lacking challenge while hoping for future expansions.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the main story and gameplay become short, repetitive, and lack meaningful endgame content or replayability after the initial hours.

citations.review_text:
[H3] Here's my review of Schedule 1 after playing for about 97 hours. [H3]

The game is fairly straight forward and intuitive making it pretty easy for anyone to get into. I would describe it as a short but fun experience. It's a open-world, crime-themed, business simulation/tycoon. If you enjoy optimizing automated operations, you'll enjoy building your drug factories. The story is alright, although I wish it was longer... like much longer. I spent about 97 hours on the game but a lot of that time was spent "stretching out" the game. I felt like I was completing/progressing too fast and eventually it got REALLY repetitive, but I think that's okay. For the price I paid, I'm confident in saying I definitely got my money's worth. BUT I do wish the game had more endgame meaningful "replayability". Of course, it's possible to continue playing and doing the tasks over and over to make more money by selling drugs, but the money/currency just ends up being a meaningless number. The game was so good for my first 70 hours or so, but after that there was nothing else to do. If you haven't played it, you should but don't expect a meaningful endgame loop.

This game is fun on your first playthrough, even getting stale by the end. This is because this game has little to no replay value. The game has been out for a while and like a lot of other games with small developers gets almost no updates at all. Their first major update after more than a year of coming out and it didn't even get me back on the game because it's just nothing. I think the reason this game has no replay value is because 1. doing a second playthrough will be the exact same as the last one except you'll probably be making money faster in the start because you know what to do. 2. The game is easier than taking candy from a baby. The thing that's supposed to give this game difficulty is the police, except it's easier to get the Fortnite Pirate Token than having a problem with the police. At night time is really the only time you need to worry about them except all they do is just stand in one spot. Because of this it is effortless to avoid them. Or if you want to you can just easily kill them. each cop will have a loaded pistol with 1 clip, you will be able to kill every cop on the map with this, but each cop has some if you need more. So the one thing that is supposed to stop you is just not there at all. The funniest thing about the major update is it was voted. It was possible to vote for harder police but I guess we need more customers. Which is the last thing we needed. It's so easy to make money with out people bulk buying. The vote was probably rigged so the devs could take the easy way out.

claims.claim: Reviewers express a desire for map expansions, higher volume buyers, and additional substance options or storyline features in future updates.

citations.review_text: Really cool game, would definitely be fun with friends. Only downside i have right now is that ive pretty much completed the game i think, and now im craving for more updates. Map extention would be sweet and so would more buyers. I think it would be awsome to have someone you can sell to in bulk. Have had fun playing this solo on my down time.

Fun game, I do believe the game is due for some more map expansion and areas, and I completely understand adding more features and small roadmap additions which completely makes sense as a game developer. It is an easy path to follow, however increasing landmass or new world access can provide further game experience. Include future stories.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe issues with in-game workers breaking or freezing, requiring frequent intervention to keep them functioning.

citations.review_text:
You can get some fun out of it but i can't recommend this game until workers are less buggy.  Everyday you have to run around watching your workers at every property you have running waiting to smack them WHEN they break, not if.  Even currently have a save where no worker at the manor will move regardless of what i do including redoing their assignments. 

Game has potential but i'd wait.

I was gifted this game by a friend

I think that this game is very fun, and it was definitely something fresh and memorable. I felt that the storyline was, perhaps, a little on the nose, but it was still very enjoyable to play through. There were a few things that I ran into over the course of the game which were a little frustrating. I didn't like that my employees could push my character model all over the place. I've been pushed through walls many times, and my tasks are often disrupted by them pushing me too far away from what I was interacting with. There needs to be better ways to automate some of the particularly mundane tasks. By the end of the game, my gameplay loop pretty much devolved into:

Wake up, place delivery orders, collect money, resupply dealers, launder, place delivery orders again, and wait to sleep / sleep.

If I could automate those tasks somehow, it would be very enjoyable to have the option to work at the locations. I think there are mods for this, but it would be interesting if these could see some kind of implementation into the base game. It's my understanding that the creator takes polls from the community about what to implement next, so its possible these things could change.

Lastly, this game is a far superior experience when had in the company of friends. It becomes a very different experience, and it can't be overstated how enjoyable it is.

Overall 8/10 ||| Solo 6/10 ||| With Friends 10/10

single_points.text: One reviewer says there is no Steam workshop and mods come from Nexus with melonloader.

citation.review_text: Good game, still early in dev so it wont take long to beat.  But i like it.  Replay ability is high due to different mix designs, different strategies and mods (unfortanitly no steam workshop, mods come from Nexus with melonloader).  Runs fine with no real issues.  After almost 400 hours I'm putting it down and will return sometime next year to check out whats new, excited to see what gets added.  As for the mods, I am blown away at the variaty and new ones have been coming out almost every day.  Great game devs, keep up the good work.  Would buy again.
